newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND DECLINE ARGENTINE OFFER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND DECLINE ARGENTINE OFFER.

text.p: Englland officials have turned down an offer from Argentina to shorten the Pumas' seven-match tour despite concern about the poor quality of the London side they will face in their opening fixture on Wednesday.

Leading players are not being released for almost all the divisional games against the tourists as part of the long- running power struggle between the Rugby Football Union and the top English clubs, forcing selectors to name a team from the lower divisions.

Against traditionally strong scrummagers such as the Pumas there are obvious safety worries, but Argentine manager Fernando Conde said his team were unconcerned by the prospect of games becoming virtual no-contests.

"We knew the problems the RFU were having and the Argentine Rugby Football Union even offered to shorten the tour," said Conde. "Eventually the RFU decided to stay with the programme, but we're not disappointed. Next month's test match will be against England's best side."
The Pumas arrived in London less than 36 hours after suffering a 44-21 defeat to South Africa in Buenos Aires without hooker Federico Mendez who has signed to play English club rugby for Bath.

The absence of Mendez, sent off as a teenager in Argentina's 51-0 defeat at Twickenham five years ago, and prop Patricio Noriega who now plays his rugby in Australia means the tourists' pack looks significantly less formidable than they were in last year's World Cup.

Talented scrum-half Augustin Pichot is a long-term injury absentee, but captain Lisandro Arbizu is hoping his squad, still amateurs despite the massive changes elsewhere in the rugby world, can still worry England.

"I've got to think about my team," he said, conceding England's professional players enjoyed a huge advantage in terms of preparation. "It's true there is a difference, but the players are putting a lot of effort in to play better, even thought they're not paid as pros."

The Pumas' main concession to rugby's new era has been to end the ban on overseas-based players in their squad. Prop Mauricio Reggiardo of French side Castres has been included with former All Black Alex "Grizz" Wyllie hired as technical advisor.
He hopes to try and beef up the Pumas' ball-winning capacity, but only five of the test side who faced South Africa are likely to be required for Wednesday's opening fixture.
